paper.title: CoSkill: Joint Reinforcement Learning of Reasoning and Meta-Skill Agents for Hierarchical Skill Evolution
paper.abstract:
Abstract Skill libraries improve the sample efficiency of agentic reinforcement learning (RL) by enabling large language model (LLM) agents to reuse procedural knowledge.
Yet existing paradigms exhibit structural shortcomings: they either decouple
skill evolution from policy optimization or instantiate meta-skills as fixed
workflows. Both treat skills as passive objects to be managed, limiting the
flexible evolution of skills and their co-adaptation with the reasoning agent.
To address the limitations, we propose CoSkill, a unified multi-agent RL
framework that recasts the static meta-skill workflow as a learnable Meta-Skill
Agent and jointly trains it with a Reasoning Agent over a hierarchical skill
library. By modeling the Reasoning and Meta-Skill Agents as a cooperative team
sharing a single backbone, CoSkill enables end-to-end co-adaptation: the
Reasoning Agent conditions its actions on a retrieved task skill and step skills
selected from its child set, while its task performance guides the Meta-Skill
Agent in refining those step skills.
Experiments on ALFWorld and WebShop show that CoSkill substantially
outperforms prior skill-based and RL baselines, achieving success rates of
98.4% and 90.6%, respectively (+3.5 and +6.2 pp). As shown in
Figure 1 , CoSkill achieves superior early-stage
sample efficiency, asymptotic performance, and wall-clock
efficiency.
Our code is available at https://github.com/jinyuan-cookie/CoSkill .

Learn more × Back to arXiv License: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 arXiv:2609.04865v1 [cs.AI] 04 Sep 2026 CoSkill: Joint Reinforcement Learning of Reasoning and Meta-Skill Agents for Hierarchical Skill Evolution Jinyuan Feng Affiliation: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences Dongmin Li Affiliation: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences Yiqun Chen Affiliation: Renmin University of China Yang Gao Affiliation: ByteDance Xing Chen Affiliation: ByteDance Huimu Wang Affiliation: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences Zhiqiang Pu Affiliation: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences Abstract Skill libraries improve the sample efficiency of agentic reinforcement learning (RL) by enabling large language model (LLM) agents to reuse procedural knowledge. Yet existing paradigms exhibit structural shortcomings: they either decouple skill evolution from policy optimization or instantiate meta-skills as fixed workflows. Both treat skills as passive objects to be managed, limiting the flexible evolution of skills and their co-adaptation with the reasoning agent. To address the limitations, we propose CoSkill, a unified multi-agent RL framework that recasts the static meta-skill workflow as a learnable Meta-Skill Agent and jointly trains it with a Reasoning Agent over a hierarchical skill library. By modeling the Reasoning and Meta-Skill Agents as a cooperative team sharing a single backbone, CoSkill enables end-to-end co-adaptation: the Reasoning Agent conditions its actions on a retrieved task skill and step skills selected from its child set, while its task performance guides the Meta-Skill Agent in refining those step skills. Experiments on ALFWorld and WebShop show that CoSkill substantially outperforms prior skill-based and RL baselines, achieving success rates of 98.4% and 90.6%, respectively (+3.5 and +6.2 pp). As shown in Figure 1 , CoSkill achieves superior early-stage sample efficiency, asymptotic performance, and wall-clock efficiency. Our code is available at https://github.com/jinyuan-cookie/CoSkill . (a) Training Curves on ALFWorld (b) Training Curves on WebShop (c) Training Efficiency Figure 1: Sample and training efficiency. CoSkill achieves higher sample efficiency on (a) ALFWorld and (b) WebShop and a stronger success–wall-clock trade-off on ALFWorld in (c). 1 Introduction Skill libraries facilitate long-horizon agentic RL by enabling LLM agents to reuse procedural knowledge across tasks. However, existing methods struggle to coordinate fine-grained skill-library optimization with reasoning-policy updates. As illustrated in Figure 2 , existing approaches fall into three paradigms, each with critical limitations that motivate a new modeling perspective. Figure 2: Skill-evolution paradigms. (a) External orchestration decouples skill evolution from policy learning. (b) RL manages skill-library operations at coarse granularity. (c) Fixed meta-skill workflows optimize individual skills without policy co-adaptation. (d) CoSkill jointly trains the Reasoning and Meta-Skill Agents for fine-grained skill–policy co-evolution. The first paradigm, Externally Orchestrated Skill Evolution (Figure 2 (a)), includes SkillRL ( Xia et al., 2026 ) , D2Skill ( Tu et al., 2026 ) , ReSkill ( He et al., 2026 ) , and Trace2Skill ( Ni et al., 2026 ) . These methods treat the skill library as a standalone knowledge base, with its generation, revision, and maintenance delegated to external LLMs or hand-crafted rules. Skill evolution therefore remains outside the policy-learning objective; as the library grows, its contents may become stale, redundant, or misaligned with the evolving reasoning policy. To reduce this optimization mismatch, the second paradigm, RL-Optimized Skill-Library Management (Figure 2 (b)), incorporates skill-library maintenance into the reinforcement learning loop. SAGE ( Wang et al., 2026a ) , ARISE ( Li et al., 2026 ) , and Skill1 ( Shi et al., 2026 ) use downstream rewards to optimize skill-lifecycle decisions, enabling the library to adapt to the evolving reasoning policy. However, this optimization remains coarse-grained: RL controls each skill’s library lifecycle but treats the skill itself as atomic, leaving its internal procedure unoptimized. Consequently, useful but imperfect skills may be underused or removed rather than refined using execution feedback. More recently, methods in the Meta-Skill-Driven Skill Optimization paradigm (Figure 2 (c)), including SkillOpt ( Yang et al., 2026 ) , EvoSkill ( Alzubi et al., 2026 ) , SkillEvolver ( Zhang et al., 2026a ) , and MetaSkill-Evolve ( Wang et al., 2026b ) , use execution feedback to shift optimization from skill-library lifecycles to individual skill procedures. However, they rely on predefined meta-skill programs (e.g., rubric-based prompts, SKILL.md specifications, or multi-agent workflows) and typically freeze the reasoning agent. Their fixed update rules cannot co-adapt with an evolving policy, reintroducing skill–policy mismatch. Learning meta-skills that co-evolve with the reasoning policy through RL therefore remains open. A broader discussion of the literature underlying these three paradigms is provided in Appendix A . In this paper, we propose CoSkill , a unified multi-agent RL framework for joint reasoning and skill evolution. CoSkill builds on a key design insight: formulating the meta-skill as an RL-trained agent rather than a fixed workflow allows its update policy to co-adapt with the reasoning policy. As illustrated in Figure 2 (d), CoSkill models the Reasoning and Meta-Skill Agents as a cooperative team sharing a single LLM backbone and jointly trains them over a hierarchical skill library. The Reasoning Agent conditions its actions on a retrieved task skill and step skills selected from its child set, while Post-Edit Skill Verification converts its task performance into outcome-aligned feedback for the Meta-Skill Agent to refine those step skills. This design directly addresses the limitations of Figure 2 (a–c): the agentic formulation both closes the skill–policy loop and replaces fixed workflows, while step-level editing moves beyond coarse library management. Together, these mechanisms enable fine-grained skill–policy co-evolution. The results in Figure 1 show that CoSkill yields superior early-stage sample efficiency, asymptotic performance, and wall-clock efficiency. 2 Preliminaries We consider an agentic RL setting in which an LLM parameterizes a policy π θ \pi_{\theta} that solves natural-language tasks x ∼ 𝒟 x\sim\mathcal{D} through sequential interaction with an environment. (2) CoSkill hierarchically retrieves task and step skills as Z t Z_{t} and jointly trains a learnable Meta-Skill Agent with the Reasoning Agent for skill–policy co-evolution. 3 Method We propose CoSkill , a unified multi-agent RL framework that casts the meta-skill as a learnable agent and jointly trains it with a Reasoning Agent over a hierarchical skill library. Section 3.1 introduces the library and its retrieval scheme, while Section 3.2 formulates shared-parameter agent interaction as an MSMDP. Sections 3.3 and 3.4 define outcome-aligned skill rewards and joint optimization via GiGPO, respectively. Figure 3 summarizes the overall framework. Figure 3: Overview of CoSkill. A task-indexed hierarchical skill library conditions the Reasoning Agent on an episode-level task skill and an observation-dependent step skill. The Meta-Skill Agent consumes each reasoning transition, proposes local step-skill edits, and writes back only revisions that improve post-edit verification. The two roles share model parameters and are optimized jointly. 3.1 Hierarchical Skill Library CoSkill structures its persistent library as ℬ = { ℬ k } k = 1 K \mathcal{B}=\{\mathcal{B}_{k}\}_{k=1}^{K} , a collection of K K task-indexed skill bundles: ℬ k = ( s k task , 𝒮 k step ) . \mathcal{B}_{k}=\left(s_{k}^{\mathrm{task}},\mathcal{S}_{k}^{\mathrm{step}}\right).
